visual_anchors.morphology_description: Single spherical compound flower head (capitulum or umbel-type). Surface covered with approximately 32 small open-circle dot marks representing individual florets. Overall shape is globose, slightly flattened at base. Diameter approximately 100 normalized units. No color wash — grey-green tint only.

Exactly 13 fine radiating brown ink lines spreading downward and outward from the base of the flower sphere, converging at the top of the main stem. Lines are evenly spaced and taper toward the stem junction.
Single unbranched main stem. No lateral branches. Runs vertically from root collar to pedicel base. Moderate width.

22 individual scalloped leaf units arranged in 3 horizontal tiers on the right side of the central stem. Each unit is a broad rounded lobe with a white highlight at the tip. Top tier: ~6 units. Middle tier: ~8 units. Lower green tier: ~8 units. Leaves point outward to the right. The overall mass has a rectangular outline.

Large rust-brown lobed mass directly below the green leaf tiers. Represents a dense root crown or rhizome. Approximately 3 large rounded lobes visible. This is the most visually prominent colored element on the folio — the saturated rust-brown contrasts strongly with the green leaves above. No distinct tuber nodes; the lobing is continuous.

Exactly 3 long sinuous root strands descending from the bottom of the brown root collar. The strands are thin, tapering, and curve gently — no branching, no tubers, no nodules. They extend down toward the bottom of the folio.

A second plant drawn behind and to the left of Plant A, rendered in a dilute blue-green wash that appears faded or intentionally 'ghosted'. The plant has 1 main stem with 2 visible lateral branches. Approximately 7 small ovate leaves are discernible. Two prominent dark blue-black flowers with open bell or trumpet shapes are positioned on the upper lateral branches. These dark-pigment flowers are the most distinctive element of Plant B.
